To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
states with a higher TRI disclosure of toxic releases in 1988 increased their 1987–1990 environmental and natural resource program expenditures more than states with lower disclosures.

states with a larger apparent pollution problem increased their resource allocations to environmental programs more than states without a larger apparent pollution problems, and that states with greater apparent pollution problems also had greater increases in resource allocation to environmental programs than states with lesser pollution problems.
states with more apparent environmental problems increased resource allocations to the environment and natural resources more than states with fewer apparent environmental problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of information disclosure on the allocation of resources by state government.
how information disclosure affects the behavior of the public and private sector.
how the EPA's disclosure program has influenced the behavior of state environmental and natural resources managers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EPA's TRI program has had a significant impact on states' resource allocations to environmental programs.
the TRI disclosure program did have a statistically significant impact on state environmental and resource expenditures, and that the program was effective in achieving its stated purpose.
states with greater apparent pollution problems based on the EPA's disclosure program did not increase their environmental spending as much as states with lesser apparent pollution problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
states with a higher level of toxic release information in the TRI disclosure program increased their environmental spending.
states with a higher apparent problem based on the EPA's 1988 TRI program increased their environmental and natural resource program expenditures in 1989 and again in 1990.
the TRI disclosure program has been an important factor in increasing state resource allocations for the environmental and natural resource areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRI data can serve as an important input for policy makers and environmental managers.
the TRI disclosure program has had some positive effects on the environmental policies of states.

TRI disclosures can have a significant effect on the allocation of resources to environmental programs, and that the impact of such disclosures is not limited to the firms that are required to report.
